steps.why: Three parts must be present for the definition to be complete: water, a difference in concentration, and a semipermeable membrane.
common_mistakes: Writing that the solute moves. In osmosis only the water moves.
Leaving out the semipermeable membrane. Without it the movement is plain diffusion.
steps.memory_tip: Osmosis is diffusion with a membrane in the way, and only water gets through.
steps.margin_note: All three parts — water, gradient, membrane — in one sentence.

steps.why: Naming osmosis as passive transport is what shows why no ATP appears anywhere in the answer.
common_mistakes: Writing that osmosis needs ATP. It is passive.
Calling osmosis active transport because a membrane is involved.
steps.memory_tip: Water moves down its own gradient, so no ATP is used.
steps.margin_note: Adding 'passive, no ATP' completes a 2-mark answer.

insider_note: Osmosis is the standard example of passive transport, so the words 'passive, no ATP' are what complete the answer.
